The keyboard shortcut tool TextExpander has introduced a free plan, allowing users to access its core Snippets feature on Mac, iPhone, iPad, Windows, and Chrome. Here are the details.

TextExpander launches free plan

I have written about TextExpander before — it's one of the first applications I install whenever I get a new Mac.

Over the years, I've built up around 200 Snippets (TextExpander calls text abbreviations that automatically expand into preset text "Snippets"), most of which I use regularly to quickly reply to emails, fill in forms, prepare podcast outlines, read sponsor mentions, write show notes, and more.

Although macOS's built-in text replacement feature continues to improve, features like fill-in variables, conditional sections, nested Snippets, and math macros still make TextExpander an indispensable tool for me.

TextExpander recently launched a free plan. According to the company speaking to 9to5Mac, the plan offers 5 active Snippets, unlimited storage, unlimited text expansions, and up to 5 team members. The free plan also works on Mac, iPhone, iPad, Windows, and Chrome, syncing the same Snippet library across devices.

The 5-Snippet limit will no doubt feel a bit restrictive, especially since the free plan only allows you to swap out one active Snippet every two weeks.

However, this can also serve as a good way to gradually adopt TextExpander — keep shorter, simpler text replacements handled by macOS, and reserve this app for longer or more complex Snippets.
